snowGrip.x-provision: Art. 4 + Annex I (3PMSF snow-grip pictogram where applicable)
snowGrip.x-citationNote: Annex I Part D requires snow grip to be tested per Annex 7 to UNECE Regulation No 117, and a tyre meeting the minimum index is classified for severe snow use and carries the 3PMSF PICTOGRAM on the tyre label. The duty is discharged by that pictogram, not by publishing a value.

iceGrip.x-citationNote: Annex I Part E requires ice grip to be tested by reliable, accurate and reproducible methods reflecting the state of the art, and a qualifying C1 tyre carries the ice-grip PICTOGRAM on the label. Like snow grip, the obligation is a mark rather than a published figure.

tyreAbrasionRateMgKm.x-citationNote: Euro 7 (Reg (EU) 2024/1257) defines tyre abrasion as the mass of material lost and emitted into the environment, and provides for abrasion LIMITS per tyre class — but those limits and their measurement method come from UN WP.29, due 1 July 2026 for C1, 1 April 2028 for C2 and 1 April 2030 for C3, with a Commission delegated act only as a fallback. There is no limit to meet and no prescribed method to report against yet.

abrasionTestMethod.title: Abrasion Test Method

abrasionTestMethod.x-citationNote: The method — convoy-on-road versus laboratory drum — is exactly what the pending UN WP.29 work under Euro 7 must settle. Naming a method today records the basis of a voluntary measurement rather than compliance with a prescribed one.

testDistanceKm.title: Test Distance (km)

microplasticsEmissionClass.title: Microplastics Emission Class

microplasticsEmissionClass.x-citationNote: Euro 7's recital ties tyre abrasion to the Union objective of reducing microplastics released into the environment by 30% by 2030, but the Regulation creates no emission CLASS for tyres. Any grading would follow the pending WP.29 limits.

The duty binds the VEHICLE's type-approval, not the tyre, and is discharged through that approval rather than through tyre product data.

dppSchemaVersion.title: DPP Schema Version
dppSchemaVersion.description: Version of the DPP schema used
dppSchemaVersion.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

lastUpdatedAt.title: Last Updated At
lastUpdatedAt.x-citationNote: ESPR Art. 10 governs the passport's TECHNICAL design — data carrier, unique identifiers, access rights, availability — not which product data must be published. The substantive obligation still arrives via an Art. 4 delegated act, and none is adopted for this category. Anticipated; voluntary today. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.
